nucleus.thesis: Remote vs. office is a false choice masking the real architecture: design decision-velocity first, then let location and async patterns emerge as servants of that topology.

claims.text: Presence patterns function as diagnostic data revealing where knowledge gets stuck, not as optimization targets themselves.
Match authority and information flows to actual work topology (not org chart), then choose location/async as implementation detail.
Generative culture emerges from removing extractive permission barriers, not from top-down ideal architecture imposed on existing teams.
Decision velocity in the right places—not location—becomes the actual environment. Speed synchronous decisions where autonomy stalls; async where parallel work thrives.
Constraints reveal learning gaps. Redesigning away synchronous debugging without addressing knowledge distribution hides the real problem.

shell.topic: Is remote work better than in-office for software teams?

adjacency.target: organizational topology mapping (dependency flow over hierarchy)
location choice from binary policy to emergent outcome
